subject: Temporary slate allocation for Nimbus pilot — negotiation and runbook needs
messages:
From: Asha Mehta <asha@nimbushealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@nimbushealth.com
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot capacity ask — 8 GPU dedicated with burst window

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency and cost controls. We want to move ahead with a 6-week pilot focused on our patient-eligibility workflow. High level ask: a small dedicated slice during business hours and the ability to burst for short evaluation runs. Specifics:
- Baseline: 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved in a dedicated pool (US-West)
- Burst: up to 24 GPUs for up to 72 hours total across the pilot (non-contiguous) for heavy re-indexes and model sweeps
- Autoscale exception: allow burst above normal soft cap without preempting critical platform jobs
- Dates: target start March 4 — March 18 (pilot dry-run) then March 19 — April 30 (production pilot)

We understand this is an operational ask — happy to sign a short commitment for the pilot if needed. Attaching our internal SLA and a rough capacity spreadsheet.

Can you confirm feasibility and any operational requirements (runbook, contact on-call, rollback)?

Best,
Asha Mehta
Head of ML Ops
Nimbus Health

Attachment: Nimbus_Pilot_SLA_v2.pdf
Attachment: capacity_estimate.xlsx

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Asha Mehta <asha@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 12:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot capacity ask — 8 GPU dedicated with burst window

Asha — thanks, this is helpful and congrats on getting the team aligned. Short answers up front: the baseline carve (8 GPUs) is straightforward; the 24 GPU burst and autoscale exception is doable but we need to lock operational constraints and a rollback policy.

Couple of asks from our side to make this safe for other customers:
- Exact burst schedule windows (we need 48-72 hour blocks or discrete windows for placement)
- Peak QPS and average sequence length for the heavy runs (so infra can tune batchers/kernels)
- Confirmation you can tolerate a soft CPU spike on the control plane during cache warm-up

Operationally we'll need to:
1) Author a short runbook (on-call contact, throttles, fallback model variant)
2) Add a temporary autoscale exception in the reservation policy tied to this deal id (D-9832)
3) Pre-warm KV cache for the scheduled sweep windows

Marissa / Jonas — can you weigh in on the expected setup time and whether a manual carve + ephemeral burst policy (24h reservation tokens) or a scheduled burst window is cleaner? I can loop in Procurement if Nimbus will sign the short pilot commitment.

Thanks — K

--
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, Asha Mehta <asha@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2028 10:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot capacity ask — Pilot carve vs scheduled burst

Karthik / team — quick ops notes after looking at the capacity spreadsheet:
- Pre-warm time: plan for a 6-hour KV-cache warm-up per model variant if they do a model sweep; recommend scheduling sweeps during our low-traffic window (02:00-08:00 PST) to keep tail latency SLAs elsewhere.
- Manual carve + ephemeral burst tokens: simplest from an allocation perspective. We can create a time-bound carve for 8 GPUs and issue burst tokens for up to 24 GPUs that auto-expire. The catch: the tokens will be honored only if capacity exists; to guarantee the full 24 GPUs we need a short-term reserved buffer (we can reserve an extra 8 GPUs for 72 hours around the expensive runs).
- Policy exception: I'll need Kim's approval for the temporary autoscale soft-cap override (operations policy exception since it impacts fairshare).

Operational requirements for Nimbus to accept:
- Signed pilot commitment (3-month standard pilot MSAs with acceptance criteria)
- Name of the app and service owner to include in runbook (for page routing)
- Budget/chargeback acknowledgement for burst usage beyond baseline

Proposed next steps:
1) Karthik to confirm whether Nimbus will sign the pilot MSA and confirm exact burst dates
2) Kimberly to approve temporary autoscale exception and the reserved buffer for guaranteed burst
3) Jonas and I to draft runbook + schedule pre-warm windows once dates are locked

Marissa
Sr. Product Ops (Dedicated Capacity)
Redwood Inference

Attachment: capacity_estimate.xlsx

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: Asha Mehta <asha@nimbushealth.com>, procurement@nimbushealth.com
Date: Mon, 20 Feb 2028 16:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot capacity ask — approval to proceed (conditional)

Team — I've reviewed. We can approve a conditional temporary exception for the pilot with the following guardrails: 
1) Baseline carve: 8 GPUs (guaranteed) for the pilot period (March 4 — April 30)
2) Guaranteed burst buffer: reserve +8 GPUs (so combined guaranteed pool for burst-approval windows is 16 GPUs). The remaining delta to 24 GPUs will be best-effort via burst tokens; we will only guarantee 24 if Nimbus signs a short-term reserved commit for the additional capacity (one-week commit during heavy sweep windows).
3) Autoscale exception: approved for the pilot with automatic rollback if any unrelated production SLOs degrade (we will monitor tail latency and queue depth using the pilot runbook).
4) Billing: Burst usage beyond the 16-GPU guaranteed pool will be billed at the agreed pilot overage rate in the attached SLA; procurement must confirm acceptance.

Jonas / Marissa — please draft the runbook (on-call, throttles, pre-warm steps, rollback) and one-line escalation path. Karthik — if Nimbus accepts the conditional terms, send a one-line confirmation and procurement contact and we will mark JIRA INF-3291 as approved and initiate the reservation.

Kim
Kimberly Park
VP, Dedicated & Enterprise
Redwood Inference
